annotation.title_clean: ИСКУССТВЕННЫЙ ИНТЕЛЛЕКТ И РОБОТОТЕХНИКА: ТЕОРЕТИКО-ПРАВОВЫЕ ПРОБЛЕМЫ РАЗГРАНИЧЕНИЯ ПОНЯТИЙНОГО АППАРАТА
annotation.title_en: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics: Theoretical and Legal Problems of Differentiating the Conceptual Apparatus
annotation.venue: Вестник Удмуртского университета. Экономика и право
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Russian legal article distinguishing 'robotics' from 'artificial intelligence' conceptually and examining whether robots or AI should be legal subjects. It favours a legal-entity analogy based on fiction theory and warns that new legal persons could reduce the accountability of professional market participants.
key_provisions_or_claims: Robotics and AI are distinct, semantically non-identical categories; AI has 'intellectuality' and self-development, robots are physical devices.
Scholars often conflate robots and AI when discussing legal status.
Legal-entity analogy under fiction theory is the most justified route to legal subjecthood.
Approaches based on real will of animate subjects will develop only once technology reaches a high level.
New legal persons may lower the responsibility of professional market participants.
